facts.raw_span: A 60‐year‐old tailor with no significant medical history
a 3‐year history of macerated skin between his toes
a painful, fissured ulcer at the base of the fourth interdigital space of the right foot
which had been progressively enlarging over the past 18 months
received multiple antifungal regimens—including topical sertaconazole for 6 weeks and oral terbinafine 250 mg daily for 6 weeks—without improvement
a verrucous, infected ulceration with infiltrated, hyperkeratotic edges and a whitish, fissured base measuring 3 cm in diameter, extending onto the dorsum of the foot
Dermoscopy revealed unstructured whitish areas and hyperkeratosis
Popliteal and inguinal lymph nodes were not palpable
the remainder of the examination was unremarkable
A 60‐year‐old tailor with no significant medical history
a 3‐year history of macerated skin between his toes
a painful, fissured ulcer at the base of the fourth interdigital space of the right foot
which had been progressively enlarging over the past 18 months
received multiple antifungal regimens—including topical sertaconazole for 6 weeks and oral terbinafine 250 mg daily for 6 weeks—without improvement
a verrucous, infected ulceration with infiltrated, hyperkeratotic edges and a whitish, fissured base measuring 3 cm in diameter, extending onto the dorsum of the foot
Dermoscopy revealed unstructured whitish areas and hyperkeratosis
Popliteal and inguinal lymph nodes were not palpable
the remainder of the examination was unremarkable

concepts.why: The presence of a painful, fissured ulcer with verrucous, infected edges and a whitish, fissured base, along with dermoscopy findings of unstructured whitish areas and hyperkeratosis, suggests a diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma.
The 3-year history of macerated skin between the toes and the presence of a painful, fissured ulcer with hyperkeratotic edges suggest a diagnosis of chronic ulcerative keratosis.

The presence of a verrucous, infected ulceration with infiltrated, hyperkeratotic edges and a whitish, fissured base, along with dermoscopy findings of unstructured whitish areas and hyperkeratosis, could also suggest a diagnosis of keratoacanthoma.

Although less likely, the presence of a painful, fissured ulcer with hyperkeratotic edges could also suggest a diagnosis of malignant melanoma, particularly if there are any pigmented areas or other suspicious features.

The presence of a painful, fissured ulcer with hyperkeratotic edges could also suggest a diagnosis of basal cell carcinoma, particularly if there are any other characteristic features such as telangiectasias or a pearly border.

rationales.F03: The presence of a painful, fissured ulcer is more typical of squamous cell carcinoma and chronic ulcerative keratosis.
rationales.F05: The lack of response to antifungal treatment suggests that the condition may not be fungal in nature, making squamous cell carcinoma and other non-fungal conditions more likely.
rationales.F06: The description of the ulceration is highly suggestive of a malignant process, such as squamous cell carcinoma.
rationales.F07: The dermoscopy findings are consistent with squamous cell carcinoma and other keratinocyte-derived tumors.
